Bootstrap the graph layer with both stages refitted

Source: R/bootstrap.R
mc_graph_bootstrap.Rd

Resamples units, or clusters of units, with replacement and refits the first-stage MCGLM and the graph layer in every resample, returning the bootstrap distribution of a statistic of the fit (by default the graph parameters and the off-diagonal partial correlations). The support of the graph is held fixed at the one the supplied fit carries, so the result is an inferential check on a given structure and not a post-selection estimator.

Usage

mc_graph_bootstrap(
  fit,
  B = 200L,
  cluster = NULL,
  statistic = NULL,
  stage = c("both", "residual"),
  level = 0.95,
  workers = 1L
)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_bootstrap'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

B

number of resamples, an integer of at least two; default 200.

cluster

optional vector with one identifier per row, with no missing values and at least two distinct values; whole clusters are resampled, with replacement, keeping the total number of clusters. Required when the within-response structure is not the identity and stage = "both".

statistic

optional function of a refitted "mcglm_graph" object returning a named numeric vector, of the same length at every resample. The default returns the graph parameters and the off-diagonal partial correlations.

stage

"both" refits the first stage and the graph layer; "residual" resamples the stored Pearson residuals and refits the graph layer alone.

level

confidence level of the percentile intervals, a number strictly between 0 and 1; default 0.95.

workers

number of parallel workers, default 1 (sequential). The resamples are drawn in the parent before any dispatch, so a given seed yields the same resamples at any worker count.

x

an object of class "mcg_bootstrap".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_bootstrap", a list with estimate, the named numeric vector of the statistic on the original sample; replicates, the B_valid by length-of-statistic matrix of valid resamples; vcov, their covariance matrix, and se, their standard deviations; bias, the mean of the replicates minus estimate; ci, the two-column matrix (lower, upper) of percentile intervals; level and stage, as given; the counts B, B_valid and B_failed; the data frame failures (replicate, error); clustered (logical) and n_clusters (NA without clusters). The print method shows the estimates, standard errors, biases and intervals and returns its argument invisibly.

Details

With \(n\) units (rows, or clusters when cluster is given), each resample draws \(n\) units with replacement (Efron, 1979), refits, and evaluates the statistic \(T(\cdot)\). With \(B_v\) valid resamples \(T^{*}_1,\dots,T^{*}_{B_v}\), the bootstrap covariance is the sample covariance of the replicates, se their standard deviations, the bias estimate \(\bar T^{*}-T(\hat{\mathrm F}_n)\), and the interval for level \(1-a\) the percentile interval with limits at the quantiles \(a/2\) and \(1-a/2\) of the replicates. A resample is dropped, and recorded with its message in failures, when its refit raises an error, when its graph layer does not converge, or when its statistic is not a finite vector of the length obtained on the original sample; the summaries use the valid resamples only, and at least two are required. Resampling independent clusters is the scheme that remains valid when rows within a cluster are dependent. Because both stages are refitted, the replicates carry the variability of the first stage, which the model-based and sandwich covariances of mc_vcov_graph take as known.

What it is for

The variances the package reports elsewhere are conditional on the estimated Pearson residuals unless the analytical correction of mc_vcov_graph is asked for. Refitting propagates the first stage by construction, for any family, which makes this the yardstick against which both routes of that correction, the shortcut and the full form, are checked. With stage = "residual" only the residuals are resampled and the first stage is held fixed, which is the comparison that isolates how much the first stage contributes.

What it requires

The first-stage call is rebuilt from the fitted object. With an identity within-response structure the rows are resampled, or whole clusters when cluster is given. A richer matrix linear predictor describes dependence among rows, so the rows it connects must be drawn together: cluster is then required, every matrix of the structure must vanish between distinct clusters, which is checked, and each drawn cluster keeps its own block of the structure. A cluster drawn twice gives two blocks that do not touch, as two independent units would; the submatrix of the rows drawn would instead join the two copies. Without cluster such a fit is refused.

References

Efron, B. (1979). Bootstrap methods: another look at the jackknife. The Annals of Statistics 7(1), 1–26. doi:10.1214/aos/1176344552

See also

mc_vcov_graph for the analytical forms and mc_graph_stability for selection frequencies.

Other resampling: mc_cpdag_stability()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 200; x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
bt <- mc_graph_bootstrap(f, B = 40)
bt$se
#>      eta_11      eta_22      eta_33      eta_12      eta_13      eta_23 
#> 0.009336896 0.012431239 0.010030779 0.082969202 0.049911598 0.069535071 
#>  pcor_y1_y2  pcor_y1_y3  pcor_y2_y3 
#> 0.080411716 0.048663508 0.067242523 
# }
